---
title: Define a type
description: Register a type for items no shipped type fits, with the properties Marfa checks on every item of it.
job: A builder registers a type for items that no shipped type fits.
kind: how-to
---

This guide registers a type for receipt photos, `app.example.receipt`, built on the image type Marfa ships. [Items and types](/build/items-and-types) explains what a type is and when to build on another. **You need** your own instance, with the CLI signed in to it, as the [Quickstart](/quickstart) leaves you.

The CLI registers with your own sign-in, which can do all of this. To register as your app instead, make it a key that may register its own types and write their items, and run the CLI commands with `MARFA_API_KEY` set to that key (the HTTP, TypeScript and Swift calls send it):

```bash
marfa keys create --label "Receipts app" --source receipts-app \
  --type-permission "app.example.*=write" --metadata-permission types=write
```

## Write the definition

Keep the definition in a file:

```json title="receipt.json"
{
  "id": "app.example.receipt",
  "parent": "core.file.image",
  "fields": {
    "merchant": { "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "Where the purchase was made" },
    "total": { "type": "number" },
    "currency": { "type": "string", "format": "currency" }
  }
}
```

- **`id`** says who the type is for: `app.<app name>.<type>` for your app's own types, `user.<type>` for types you keep for yourself, or a name of your own, such as `acme.deal`, for types you publish. Name a type with a singular noun, in `snake_case`. [Type definition](/catalog/type-definition#identifier) lists what an identifier must meet.
- **`parent`** makes the type a child of another. A receipt is an image with a merchant and a total, so it takes every property of `core.file.image`.
- **`fields`** declares the type's own properties. Each needs a `type`, one of the [field kinds](/catalog/field-kinds). A property can't share a name with a field every item has, such as `source` or `version` ([reserved names](/catalog/type-definition#fields)).

[Register a type](/reference/api/types/registerType) lists the rest a definition can hold, such as display hints, policies and [tables](/build/tables). **Marfa keeps a property the type doesn't declare**; to refuse one, name the type in the `strict_mode` lever ([Settings](/reference/instance-settings#enforcement-levers)).

`marfa types scaffold app.example.receipt --parent core.file.image --field merchant:string --required merchant` prints a definition to start from, with an empty `description` to fill in. It needs no server or key, and refuses what registration would refuse.

To tell agents how to fill a type, keep Markdown beside its definition, as `recipe.md` beside `recipe.json`, and the CLI sends it as the type's [guidance](/catalog/type-definition#descriptions-and-guidance). An `app.*` type, such as the receipt, takes none. [Check type definitions](/build/check-type-definitions) checks a folder before you register any.

## Register the type

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa types register --file receipt.json
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /types
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

<the contents of receipt.json>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const definition = JSON.parse(await readFile("receipt.json", "utf8"));
const { data, error } = await marfa.POST("/types", { body: definition });
```

```swift tab="Swift"
import Foundation
import MarfaAPI

let api = Client(server)
let definition = try JSONDecoder().decode(
    Components.Schemas.TypeDefinitionInput.self, from: Data(contentsOf: receiptURL))
let registered = try await api.register(itemType: definition)
```

In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows. In the Swift examples, `api` is a `Client` made as [the Swift SDK](/reference/swift-sdk#the-api-client) shows. Marfa answers `201` with the type as it stored it:

```json title="Response" status="201"
{
  "id": "app.example.receipt",
  "version": 0,
  "fields": {
    "merchant": { "type": "string", "description": "Where the purchase was made", "required": true },
    "total": { "type": "number" },
    "currency": { "type": "string", "format": "currency" }
  },
  "parent": "core.file.image",
  "label": "Receipt",
  "plural": "Receipts",
  "provenance": {
    "origin": "user",
    "created_by": { "kind": "key", "id": "01a1f12f-c7d0-7a21-9f6b-4d2c8e1a3b57", "name": "Receipts app" }
  }
}
```

Marfa made the `label` and `plural` from the identifier. The `version` is **yours to keep:** Marfa stores the number you send, 0 when you send none, and never changes it.

**An item must hold every required property along the chain,** so a receipt needs a `blob_ref`, a `mime_type` and a `merchant`. `marfa types get app.example.receipt` shows the type with the properties it inherits. A write that lacks one is refused `400 invalid_properties`, naming it.

## What your key needs

Registering takes write on the type's identifier and `metadata.types:write`, the `types` entry of the key's metadata map. Replacing a type takes the same when the change only adds optional properties no item holds a value under, or changes labels, descriptions, display hints or the version; any other change takes the `schema.write` permission, and so does deleting, with write on the type. **Guidance takes `schema.write` too,** to register a type with it or to add, change or remove it. A missing write is refused `403 type_not_permitted`, and a call that needs `schema.write` from a key without it, `403 forbidden` with `details.changes` naming each part. [Manage keys](/use/manage-keys) shows how to give a key its maps and permissions.

Once it's registered, [change, rename or delete it](/build/change-a-type) as your app grows. The rules behind this guide are in the [types](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/types.md) chapter of the contract.
